Hatz AI raises $24Mn Series A to sell AI through MSPs
Danica Macayan
Posted on November 17, 2026 2 min read
Copied URL
Key facts
Hatz AI raised $24 million in Series A funding.
Josh Schertzer of Nadia Partners led the deal.
Hatz’s active MSP partner count tripled year over year.
Hatz grew from 14 to nearly 60 employees.
Source: Hatz AI
NEW YORK, UNITED STATES — Hatz AI, which sells its artificial intelligence (AI) platform to small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) only through managed service providers (MSPs), has raised $24 million in Series A funding. Nadia Partners, Vestigo Ventures and The Private Shares Fund backed the round.
Josh Schertzer, a partner at Nadia Partners and former chief technology officer at Blackstone, led the deal.
AI sold under the MSP’s brand
Hatz announced the funding in a press release on Nov. 12.
Its platform gives MSPs multi-tenant AI governance, custom workflows and automated routing across leading foundation models. MSPs can then package and deliver AI-as-a-Service under their own brand.
Hatz said it has no competing direct-to-enterprise sales and has issued more than 15,000 AI certifications to builders globally.
The investment will help it scale a partner network that it said spans thousands of MSPs in all 50 U.S. states, nine Canadian provinces and nine countries.
Partners triple, staff quadruple
Hatz said its active MSP partner count tripled year over year, while revenue grew even faster. It expanded its workforce from 14 to nearly 60 employees.
The company is expanding in Flatiron, New York City, and scaling its forward deployed engineer team to work alongside partners. It is also growing its AI research and AI optimization teams.
“Small businesses represent the backbone of the global economy, and the managed service providers they already rely on are exactly the people to lead this transformation,” said Jimmy Hatzell, chief executive and co-founder of Hatz AI.
“By giving MSPs full control over governance, spend, and deployment, we’re making it possible for every small business to become AI native,” Hatzell said.
What the money funds
The new capital will deepen platform capabilities, including Hatz’s auto-model routing engine, benchmarks and internal software factory infrastructure. Hatz will also keep recruiting engineers for its forward deployed engineering and AI research units.
“By focusing exclusively on powering MSPs rather than trying to sell directly to end-users, Hatz has built a true dominance in channel-delivered AI,” Schertzer said.
What it means for buyers
Investors are backing a model in which smaller companies get AI from the IT provider they already pay, rather than from the model makers directly. For businesses that buy managed services or information technology outsourcing (ITO) , that puts AI governance and spending decisions into an existing contract.

o15 Capital Partners Provides Unitranche Facility and Equity Co-Investment to Support Bluestone Equity Partners' Acquisition of 11th St. Workshop
News provided by
o15 Capital Partners
Nov 17, 2026, 11:45 ET
Share this article
Share this article
ATLANTA , Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- o15 Capital Partners ("o15"), through its Emerging America Credit Opportunities ("EACO") fund, is pleased to announce a senior secured "last-out" term loan as part of a $23.6 million unitranche facility, along with an equity co-investment, to support the acquisition of 11 th St. Workshop by Bluestone Equity Partners ("Bluestone").
11 th St. Workshop is a leading design and fabrication platform that builds the physical environments behind marquee brand activations for blue-chip agency and brand customers.
"11th St. Workshop has built a differentiated platform at the intersection of creative design and highly specialized physical execution, supported by a blue-chip customer base and a reputation for delivering complex, high-profile activations," said Harry Savage, Principal at o15. "We're excited to partner with the Bluestone and 11th St. Workshop teams as the Company builds a leading national platform."
The transaction reflects o15's focus on partnering with experienced sponsors to provide flexible capital to high-quality lower-middle-market businesses with differentiated market positions and compelling opportunities to scale. Bluestone's investment will support 11th St. Workshop's next phase of growth through investments in capacity and service offerings while maintaining its reputation for quality and customer service.
"Experiential marketing is one of the fastest-growing areas of advertising spend, and 11th St. Workshop is a trusted partner for agencies and brands on their most high-profile builds," said Shaaz Khan, Senior Vice President at Bluestone. "The o15 team delivered a flexible financing package to support our acquisition, and we look forward to partnering with them to enable the Company's long-term growth."
About o15 Capital Partners
Based in Atlanta, o15 Capital Partners is an alternative investment firm that provides growth capital to undercapitalized lower-middle-market businesses and communities in the Healthcare, Education and Business Services industries.

articles.title: With $23M in funding, Luminal is the latest startup to put Nvidia's CUDA moat in its crosshairs
articles.snippet: With $23M in funding, Luminal is the latest startup to put Nvidia's CUDA moat in its crosshairs SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
UPDATED 10:00 EST / NOVEMBER 12 2026
INFRA
With $23M in funding, Luminal is the latest startup to put Nvidia’s CUDA moat in its crosshairs
by Mike Wheatley
Luminal AI Inc. has outlined a plan to tear down Nvidia Corp.’s formidable software moat in the artificial intelligence chip industry after raising $23 million in early-stage funding.
Today’s Series A round was led by Standard Capital and saw participation from existing investors such as Y Combinator, SagaVC, Liquid 2 and Felicis, bringing Luminal’s total amount raised to date to more than $28 million. It comes about a year after the startup raised $5.3 million in seed funding.
Everybody knows about Nvidia these days. The chipmaker has ridden the generative AI wave to a staggering $5 trillion market valuation, surpassing rivals such as Apple Inc., Alphabet Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. to become the most valuable publicly traded company in the world. But anyone who assumes that it’s solely Nvidia’s graphics processing units that set it apart would be mistaken, for the real reason for its dominance of the AI computing industry is not just silicon, but software.
For almost two decades, Nvidia’s proprietary Compute Unified Device Architecture or CUDA software framework has been the real differentiator, serving as a virtually impenetrable barrier that prevents rivals such as Advanced Micro Devices Inc., Google LLC and Amazon Web Services Inc. from stripping away its market lead. Though those rivals have developed some very powerful GPUs and custom application-specific integrated circuits for running AI workloads at lower costs than Nvidia’s hardware, they haven’t been able to match the scale of Nvidia’s software ecosystem.
Virtually every major AI framework, including TensorFlow and PyTorch, has been built natively on Nvidia’s CUDA software, enabling developers to run their AI models on Nvidia’s GPUs without any modifications. But to run their models on alternative chips, developers need to rewrite much of the underlying code, which is challenging and time-consuming work. That’s why the vast majority of AI workloads still run on Nvidia’s chips.
Many developers don’t want to be paying the exorbitant fees needed to rent Nvidia’s GPUs or purchase them outright, but they also don’t want to spend months at a time fine-tuning their codebases to get their AI models to run optimally on alternative hardware, and it’s this challenge that Luminal intends to solve for them.
The startup’s solution is a two-pronged architecture platform that consists of its proprietary search compiler and a fully managed inference cloud that combine to eliminate the hassles of bringing AI workloads onto different chips.
Co-founder and Chief Executive Joe Fioti told SiliconANGLE that the compiler works by systematically exploring different ways of running neural networks on the target chip in order to come up with the most optimal path. It benchmarks each variation until it finds the best possible solution, and then it automatically generates the code developers need.
Once the code is ready, it caches the implementation so it can be reused across recurring inference workloads. In this way, it allows developers to run their AI applications across heterogeneous chip architectures with minimal fuss, Fioti said.

Melbourne adtech Vudoo has raised $22 million in a Series B as it looks to scale in the US
The round was led by US fund Blue Sky Capital, supported by several existing family office investors.
The funds will go on expanding its overseas sales operations and developing its commerce technology.
Vudoo has hired two executives to lead its North American push as it looks to get more retailers selling directly through ads and videos.
Vudoo was founded in 2017 by Nick Morgan and Andrew Spalding, who conceived the interactive videos idea while chatting in a Singapore bar. One of its earliest checkouts appeared in a 2022 Vogue Australia campaign with News Corp Australia for Moët & Chandon. Viewers watching model Victoria Lee put together a birthday celebration could buy a personalised bottle of champagne inside the video, then continue watching

It gives publishers audience retention and advertiser the ability to track what someone bought after watching an ad. Tha champagne house reported shoppers who took up the video offers spent an average of $140, compared with a typical $90 online.
Morgan, Vudoo’s CEO, sees a similar opportunity as people begin discovering products through AI.
“Commerce is moving beyond traditional storefronts, with the transaction moment shifting into the media, content and AI environments where consumers discover and engage with products,” he said.
“We made a deliberate decision to build Vudoo for that future.”
Vudoo has promoted Isabella Spragg to chief operating officer to oversee its global operations. Spragg recently joined as global director of ad infrastructure and partnerships, following senior roles at The Trade Desk and Monks during a 20-year career.
In New York, 20-year ad veteran Tash Henderson takes charge of North American commercial operations as MD, having previously worked at News Corp Australia and iHeartMedia’s Unified.
Former H&M Group and Bambuser executive Sophie Abrahamsson joins as North American head of retail, alongside Julian Colantuono as customer success director, overseeing Vudoo’s work with clients globally.
